text:
Alice: heads-up — CI perf job `perf/latency-main` spiked after merge 0c9f8a2 (kernel selector tweaks). failures across AMD/GPU matrix.
Cheng: ugh, saw that. failing tests show massive compile times + higher p90. any obvious logs?
Alice: paste from CI:
```
ci-bench: compile_time_ms=1200 -> 8200
ci-bench: kv_cache_misses=0.02 -> 0.48
ci-bench: selected_kernel=full_unfused_fastpath_oob
```
Cheng: selected_kernel looks wrong — should have picked fused_lowmem for these shapes. autotune is picking a new candidate after the heuristic change.
Mike: I reproduced locally on A100 repro: same compile storm when multiple small requests hit after scale-up. nvprof shows many JIT compilations.
sre-bot: perf/latency-main failed 3 runs in a row. See https://ci.internal/perf/1753001122 
Ryan: does the change invalidate kernel cache keys? I remember a recent key-namespace rename in the compilation layer.
Eve: yep — the patch renamed kernel_key_v2 -> kernel_key_v3 and we forgot to migrate persisted entries. fallback triggers a full recompile and then autotune tries many variants.
Cheng: that explains the kv_cache_misses increase. When cache entries absent, runtime runs autotune candidates sequentially which caused the compile storm.
Alice: impact: hosted customers saw transient p95 increases ~250ms for a short window during the rollout. Dedicated nodes hit capacity because of compile CPU spikes.
Mike: quick mitigation: we can hotfix by mapping v3 -> v2 keys at lookup time (compat shim) so cached kernels are used. small diff, low risk.
Ryan: alternatively, a fast revert of the key-rename commit would stop new nodes from emitting v3 keys, but existing nodes already missed. shim seems better short-term.
Eve: I prepared a patch for shim, will push in 10m. also adding a guard to prevent autotune from trying >2 candidates concurrently in warmup mode.
Cheng: also add a metric for "autotune_trials_per_request" and alert if >3 to detect reselection storms.
Alice: can we also throttle JIT concurrency in CI to avoid flaking perf jobs while we sort this?
sre-bot: created incident INC-2026 to track kinetic compile storms.
Mike: bisect notes — suspected bad commit is 0c9f8a2 (kernel heuristic refactor) and follow-up rename 1a2b3c4. will bisect if shim doesn't stabilize.
Eve: pushed shim -> staging (deploy id: deploy-788). monitoring shows compile_time_ms drop back to baseline on staging.
Cheng: nice. create postmortem and add integration test that simulates missing cache keys + warmup traffic to catch this.
Alice: agreed. also add a CI perf job that runs with key-migration toggled to detect regressions in future.
Ryan: long-term: we should version cache keys + include model+seq_length+quantization fingerprint to avoid namespace collisions.
Mike: logging: add a one-line audit when autotune picks a different kernel than last-known for a model fingerprint. makes followups easier.
Eve: will open PRs: shim, autotune cap, metric, logging, test. linking PRs in INC-2026.
Alice: thanks everyone. i'll hold the rollout on main until we confirm stable in staging for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
Cheng: if shim fixes prod, we can do a minimal revert later. otherwise full revert. either way let's not roll out more kernel-selection changes this week.
Ryan: noted.
Eve: pushed production shim at 1753002380 — initial telemetry looks good, p95 restored. will keep monitoring.
Alice: closing thread for now, followups in INC-2026 and PRs.
